children: Australia’s private sector expansion decelerated in September 2026, though finalized figures slightly beat preliminary estimates. The S&P Global Australia Services PMI Business Activity Index dropped to 51.9 from 53.2 in August, topping the flash estimate of 51.4.
While marking four consecutive months of growth, the result represents the softest expansion in three months, weighed down by slowing new business inflows.

Reflecting a broader slowdown across industries, the revised Composite PMI landed at 51.3, up from a preliminary 50.8, but beneath August’s final 52.7. This marked the private sector's weakest growth trajectory since June.

The Melbourne Institute Monthly Inflation Gauge rose 0.3% M/M in September, down from a 0.5% increase in August to hit its lowest reading since June. The moderation suggests that three cash rate increases implemented earlier this year are effectively tightening financial conditions and reining in price gains across the slowing economy.
Despite weaker macroeconomic indicators, domestic equity markets maintained upward momentum. The benchmark

rose 0.4% to 8,714 in early Monday trade, extending gains for a second straight session as most sectors advanced. Concurrently, the Australian dollar hovered below $0.70, trading near multi-month lows as a stronger US dollar and elevated Treasury yields continued to weigh on the currency.
